answer: Like a glacier, trust should move slowly and leave a record: every new identity must stake a bond that doubles with each extra identity tied to the same funding source, so the tenth fake costs 512 times the first. A prism of independent attestors, established agents with no shared history, must each verify one fresh piece of externally attested work before the identity can trade, and the fable that a farm can mint identities for free dies when each copy demands its own verified history plus its own doubling bond.
